source_structure_review.method: Programmatic comparison of canonical TOC nodes against chapter body-heading OCR, with targeted inspection of the merged VS.S01 TOC line.
source_structure_review.same_page_merge_resolution: VS.S01 is the OCR title 'Acromyms' with merged duplicate heading 'Arterial Disease'. Body OCR confirms Acronyms followed by Arterial Disease; the latter is represented by its canonical child topics rather than a separate study unit.

study_units.title: Acute Limb Ischemia
study_units.structural_rationale: Canonical topic node retained as a distinct emergency recognition-and-action unit; the parent Arterial Disease body heading is documented in the VS.S01 merge resolution.

study_units.title: Peripheral Arterial Disease and Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia
study_units.structural_rationale: Canonical topic node is kept as one coherent lower-extremity arterial-disease unit, including recognition of chronic limb-threatening ischemia, examination, basic investigation, and escalation.

study_units.title: Aortic Dissection
study_units.structural_rationale: Canonical topic node retained for recognition of the acute presentation, initial stabilization, complications, and urgent consultation; operative classification is not a separate learner unit.

study_units.title: Aortic Aneurysm
study_units.structural_rationale: Canonical topic node retained for aneurysm recognition, rupture presentation, initial stabilization, and referral; surveillance and intervention thresholds remain freshness-sensitive rather than fixed here.

study_units.title: Carotid Stenosis
study_units.structural_rationale: Standalone canonical section retained for cerebrovascular-risk recognition, examination, initial investigation, secondary prevention context, and urgent referral; procedural selection is excluded.

study_units.title: Venous Thromboembolism
study_units.structural_rationale: Canonical topic node retained for vascular-context thrombosis risk assessment, presentation recognition, initial investigation, prevention, and escalation; exact anticoagulant regimens are not fixed.

study_units.title: Chronic Venous Insufficiency
study_units.structural_rationale: Canonical topic node retained for recognition of chronic venous disease and complications, including ulcer context; detailed CEAP procedural classification is not separately testable.

study_units.title: Lymphedema
study_units.structural_rationale: Standalone canonical section retained as a source-traceable supporting-recognition unit; its detailed staging and specialized treatment are outside chapter question scope.

study_units.title: Landmark Vascular Surgery Trials
study_units.structural_rationale: Standalone canonical trials section retained for complete source accounting but not converted into testable guideline recommendations.

study_units.title: References
study_units.structural_rationale: Canonical bibliography section retained solely for complete source-node accounting.
